title: Door Lock Control Switch: Removal and Refitting
introduction:
The little lock button sits in a much larger access job: the front door trim panel comes off before the switch’s retaining clips can be released. I use the rear-view inset like the underside of a snap-lid box—it shows where the catches hold, so the release comes before the pull.

This guide covers removal and refitting, including the trim-panel and window-switch access details and the trim-fastener tightening specifications. It does not diagnose an electrical lock fault.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Park the car, apply the parking brake and leave it on its wheels. Disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around the vehicle. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started at any time, resulting in personal injury or death. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from accidentally starting the engine during service; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Protect eyes, ears and hands
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling parts with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to follow these precautions may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Trim-release and tightening equipment
items.detail: Have a trim-removal wedge and torque equipment suitable for the trim-panel fasteners: the upper and center bolts each take 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm); the lower retainers take 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm). Keep these groups separate—the small retainers are not auditioning for the big-bolt torque. These values come from [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600).

items.name: Keep the access drawings available
items.detail: Use [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600) for the panel attachment locations and release order, and [Front Door Window Control Switch](#/document/G1695936) for removing the window-switch and bezel assembly. The panel drawings show the opposite door from the lock-switch drawing; the accompanying procedures identify the other side as similar.

edits.text: Remove the Door Lock Control Switch
NOTE: Left-hand drive (LHD) is shown; right-hand drive (RHD) is similar.
edits.why: The illustration establishes the layout for the shown driving configuration; use the corresponding locations on the other configuration.

edits.text: NOTE: The left-hand (LH) side is shown; the right-hand (RH) side is similar.
edits.why: Match the switch and its attachments to the door being serviced rather than treating the picture’s left and right as universal.

edits.text: Remove the front door trim panel. Refer to: [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600) (501-05 Interior Trim and Ornamentation, Removal and Installation).
edits.why:
Removing the panel exposes the back of the lock switch and its retaining clips. The access order matters because the panel is held by bolts, clips and pin-type retainers, then remains connected by the latch cable and any fitted electrical connectors.

Begin by removing the cover in the interior handle recess and the upper trim-panel bolt. Next remove the front door window control switch and bezel assembly using [Front Door Window Control Switch](#/document/G1695936): use a trim-removal wedge to release the attachments of the long window-switch bezel on the armrest, lift the switch and bezel out together, and disconnect its electrical connector. Leave the window switch attached to its bezel for this lock-switch job; the assembly can be set aside intact.

With the window-switch assembly out, remove the trim-panel center bolt, then the lower retainers. At the rear upper portion of the panel, release the clip followed by the pin-type retainers and move that portion away from the door. Continue around the rear and lower portion by releasing the pin-type retainer followed by the clip. At the front edge, release the lower pin-type retainer followed by the upper pin-type retainers.

Once these attachments are released, lift the panel up and out. Disconnect the electrical connectors if equipped, then release the latch cable to free the panel. A panel that still holds at an attachment needs that attachment released, not a stronger tug.

edits.text: Remove the door lock control switch using the clip-release sequence below.
edits.why: The switch is retained in the trim panel from behind. The inset shows the retaining mechanism; the main view shows the direction in which the released switch leaves its opening.

edits.text: From the back of the removed trim panel, release the door lock control switch retaining clips shown in the inset.
edits.why: Work from behind the handle surround, beside the interior door-release handle. Release the retaining catches before trying to move the switch through the opening; a stubborn catch wants releasing, not a demonstration of your gym membership.

edits.text: With the retaining clips released, remove the door lock control switch from its opening in the direction shown.
edits.why: Withdraw the released switch through its opening toward the finished face of the trim panel. The rear-view inset shows the catches; the main view shows the switch leaving the face of the handle surround.

edits.text: Refit the Door Lock Control Switch
Install the door lock control switch and front door trim panel by reversing the removal sequence.
edits.why:
Seat the switch in its opening and engage its retaining clips before returning the panel to the door. Reverse the panel connections by attaching the latch cable and reconnecting the electrical connectors if equipped, then reverse the panel’s up-and-out removal movement and re-engage its attachments.

Refit the lower retainers to 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm), and the center bolt to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm), as specified in [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600). Reconnect and refit the window-switch and bezel assembly by reversing [Front Door Window Control Switch](#/document/G1695936), then refit the upper trim-panel bolt to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm) and replace the cover. If the trim panel is being replaced, transfer parts as necessary before installation. The mechanical completion points are a retained switch, restored cable and connector attachments, and a seated trim panel with its fasteners tightened to their respective specifications.

Ordinary completion check: with the door fully assembled and the car still parked with its parking brake applied, keep the key accessible and check that the replaced switch requests both locking and unlocking. Confirm the interior handle releases the latch normally. For the restored window switch, bring the valid key into the cabin and switch the ignition ON with the engine stopped: keep the brake and clutch pedals released, then press and release the keyless start/stop button. Keep hands and objects clear of the glass and check normal window-switch operation. Finish by keeping both pedals released and pressing/releasing the button to switch the ignition OFF. Remove the key before any further connector inspection. These are post-assembly controls checks, not electrical fault isolation; resolve abnormal operation before driving. The ignition-only method follows the Mustang Owner’s Manual, Keyless Starting section.
